description: OutFin, produced by Fahad Alhomayani and Mohammad H. Mahoor, records outdoor location fingerprints for testing positioning methods. Two smartphones measured WiFi, Bluetooth and cellular signal strengths alongside magnetic, acceleration, rotation, pressure and ambient-light observations. The repository describes four dispersed sites with 122 reference points and different point spacing. An interactive collection map provides ground-truth and phone-estimated coordinates, site photographs, building heights and ground elevation. Figshare version 2 was published in October 2020 as a ZIP package under CC BY 4.0, with free access. The inspected own metadata does not specify a complete measurement period, common sampling interval or internal file-format inventory. Separate Python validation scripts are available under MIT. These observations can calibrate outdoor positioning and sensor-fusion components in mobility or infrastructure digital twins, alongside radio-network models such as model-vienna-5g-simulators. Two phones and four selected sites cannot represent all hardware, weather or urban geometries; transfer and time synchronisation require checking against the released documentation.
